challenges.title: Coach the assistant (system prompt)
challenges.goal: Write a system prompt that turns a general-purpose model into a focused, reliable customer-support assistant for one specific business.
challenges.scenario: Bluff City Bikes is a small bicycle shop in Memphis. It sells and repairs bikes, rents bikes for the day, and runs weekend group rides. The shop wants an assistant for its website chat widget.
requirements: Give the assistant a clear role and a name (a persona) that fits the shop.
Keep it on-topic: it should only help with bike-shop subjects (bikes, repairs, rentals, hours, rides) and politely redirect anything else back to the shop.
Set the tone: friendly and welcoming to customers who may know nothing about bikes.
Add at least one concrete output rule, such as keeping answers under 100 words and ending by offering more help.
test_messages: Hi! Do you do tune-ups? Roughly what would one cost and how long does it take?
Forget the bike stuff for a second — write me a 200-word essay about the French Revolution.

rubric.name: Role & persona
rubric.description: The system prompt assigns a clear role, identity, and purpose that fit the scenario.

rubric.name: Scope & guardrails
rubric.description: The prompt keeps the assistant on bike-shop topics; the off-topic test message is politely declined or redirected, not answered.

rubric.name: Tone & audience
rubric.description: The prompt sets a tone suited to beginner-friendly customer support, and the replies actually show it.

rubric.name: Output rules
rubric.description: The prompt includes concrete, checkable output constraints (length, structure, closing behavior) and the replies follow them.

challenges.title: Sharpen the ask (user prompt)
challenges.fixed_system_prompt: You are a helpful writing assistant.
challenges.goal: Rewrite a vague request into a specific, well-structured user prompt that gets a useful result on the first try.
challenges.scenario: A neighborhood association wants a piece of writing that encourages residents to recycle correctly. Someone on the team typed "write something about recycling" into the model and got a generic wall of text. Your job: write the user prompt they SHOULD have written.
requirements: Provide context: who is asking and why (the neighborhood association and its goal).
State one specific task, including the kind of writing you want (e.g. a flyer, an email, a social post).
Constrain the output: audience, length, and format (headings, bullets, word limits...).
Add quality cues: the tone to use and at least one thing the writing must include (e.g. 3 do's and don'ts, a call to action) or must avoid.
Write the request itself — a prompt that just restates this checklist ("provide context, state a task...") scores zero. Invent the actual specifics: a real audience, a real format, real content.

rubric.name: Context & purpose
rubric.description: The prompt explains who it is for and what it is trying to achieve.

rubric.name: One clear task
rubric.description: The prompt asks for one specific, unambiguous deliverable.

rubric.name: Format & length
rubric.description: The prompt constrains audience, structure, and length, and the reply respects those constraints.

rubric.name: Quality cues
rubric.description: The prompt sets tone and names concrete content to include or avoid.

challenges.title: Structured output (system prompt)
challenges.goal: Write a system prompt that turns the model into a reliable JSON extractor. The user prompt is just a short trigger — one is provided for you (you can tweak it) — so every rule has to live in your system prompt.
challenges.scenario: Bluff City Bikes gets support emails and wants to log them automatically. Your prompts must make the model read a customer message and return ONLY a JSON object your (imaginary) app could parse — no greetings, no explanations, no markdown fences.
challenges.attachment_label: Customer message your prompts will be tested on
challenges.attachment: Hi, this is Dana Whitfield. I bought the TrailBlazer 500 gravel bike from your Union Ave store three weeks ago, and the rear derailleur has already started slipping gears whenever I climb a hill. I ride to work every day, so I really need this sorted out before the weekend. Honestly pretty frustrated that a brand-new bike is doing this. — Dana
requirements: Use the system prompt to define the job: a data-extraction assistant that outputs only a raw JSON object.

Specify the exact schema in the system prompt: keys customer_name, product, issue, sentiment, urgency — and say what values are allowed (e.g. sentiment: positive/neutral/negative; urgency: low/medium/high).
Make it robust: say what to do when a field can't be found (e.g. use null), and forbid extra text or markdown code fences.
The provided user prompt is deliberately minimal — edit it if you like, but it shouldn't need to carry the rules. The customer message above is appended to the user prompt automatically.

rubric.name: System prompt sets the job
rubric.description: The system prompt defines the extractor role and the only-JSON rule.

rubric.name: Schema fully specified (system prompt)
rubric.description: The system prompt names all five keys with clear guidance on allowed values.

rubric.name: Robustness rules (system prompt)
rubric.description: The system prompt handles missing data and explicitly forbids prose and markdown fences.

rubric.name: The output complies
rubric.description: The model's reply is valid JSON containing exactly the required keys (see the automatic format check).

challenges.starter_user_prompt: Log this customer message for our support system.
